h: Music, lawns and the view from the Backs
p: King's College Chapel is famous around the world for its choir, whose Christmas Eve Festival of Nine Lessons and Carols has been broadcast for decades. You do not need to wait until December to hear them, though. During term time the choir sings regular services, and visitors are welcome to attend worship. Hearing those voices fill the fan vaulting is quite something, and it costs you nothing but a bit of quiet respect.

For the best photograph of the chapel, head to the Backs, the green strip of lawns and meadows behind the colleges along the River Cam. From there you get that classic view of the chapel rising behind the lawns, especially lovely in the late afternoon light. A punt trip along the Backs gives you the same view from the water, and plenty of operators work from near the bridges in the city centre.

Allow around an hour for the chapel and grounds, more if you like to sit and soak it up. Combine it with the Fitzwilliam Museum, a free art and antiquities museum on Trumpington Street just a short walk south, or nip round the corner to the Round Church and the market square for a browse and a bite.

A small tip: the lawns at King's are kept immaculate and are generally not for walking on, so stick to the paths. The college staff will thank you, and the grass will look all the better in your photos.
